- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.2) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >72.5), leading to overcorrection in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment in next forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.2), model often fails to capture mean reversion; align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of historical prices.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; dampen initial forecast by 1–3%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +0.4 and -0.2), model overfits short-term noise; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% sentiment, 30% price history).
